skill.name: task-execution-engine
skill.description: Executes implementation task lists stored in Markdown design documents, using checkbox status, priorities, dependencies, and a local task manager script.
skill.summary: Run, resume, and update Markdown implementation tasks from design documents.
skill.author: notedit

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown code fences, inline task attributes, and regex patterns. No shell or Ruby backtick execution was found. One medium issue remains because the helper reads and rewrites any supplied file path without validation.

remediation.suggestion: Resolve the provided file path and restrict it to trusted project design directories before reading or writing.
Add a dry-run mode and create a backup before done or fail commands rewrite Markdown files.

remediation.issue: External helper usage depends on trusted input files
remediation.suggestion: Document that users should inspect design files before running unattended implementation workflows.

semantic_findings.title: Unrestricted Task File Path
semantic_findings.description: The helper accepts a file path from the command line and reads or rewrites that path without validation. A mistaken or malicious task file argument could modify files outside the intended design directory.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The code directly uses args.file for read_text and write_text in task commands. This is intended behavior, but no path allowlist or project-boundary check is present.

content.value_statement: Implementation plans often stall when tasks are tracked outside the design document. This skill reads Markdown checklists, selects the next task, and updates progress in place.
actual_capabilities: Parses Implementation Tasks sections from Markdown files.
Selects the next pending task by priority after dependencies are complete.
Marks tasks completed, failed, or pending with checkbox updates.
Summarizes completed, pending, blocked, and failed task counts.
Outputs task details as text or JSON through the helper script.
limitations: It only understands the documented Markdown checkbox format.
It does not validate whether implementation code is correct.
It can rewrite any file path provided to the helper script.
It does not create backups before updating task files.

use_cases.title: Resume a Feature Build
use_cases.description: Continue from the first unfinished task in a design document after an interrupted coding session.

use_cases.title: Coordinate Batch Implementation
use_cases.description: Run a prioritized task list while tracking completed, blocked, and failed work in one Markdown file.

use_cases.title: Track Design-Driven Work
use_cases.description: Keep implementation status beside requirements, target files, and acceptance criteria.

prompt_templates.title: Start the Next Task
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner workflow for one design document.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use task-execution-engine with docs/designs/user-auth.md. Show the next available task before editing files.

prompt_templates.title: Resume Interrupted Work
prompt_templates.scenario: Continue a partially completed implementation plan.
prompt_templates.prompt: Resume implementation from docs/designs/user-auth.md. Continue from the first pending task and update checkbox status after each result.

prompt_templates.title: Run With Verification
prompt_templates.scenario: Execute tasks and record failures clearly.
prompt_templates.prompt: Run tasks from docs/designs/billing.md in dependency order. After each task, run relevant tests and mark failures with a short reason.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Then Continue
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced recovery for a mixed task state.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review docs/designs/search.md, summarize completed, pending, blocked, and failed work, then implement the highest-priority unblocked task.

output_examples.input: Run the next task from docs/designs/user-auth.md.
output: Next task selected: Create User model.
Files to inspect: src/models/user.py and tests/models/test_user.py.

output_examples.input: Resume implementation after an interrupted session.
output: Blocked tasks wait until dependencies are complete.
The first available pending task is started.

output_examples.input: Mark the current task as failed with a reason.
output: The task checkbox is marked as finished with a failure marker.
The reason is written under the task.
Remaining tasks can still continue when dependencies allow.

best_practices: Review the design document before starting unattended execution.
Keep task titles stable because dependencies reference task titles.
Create a checkpoint before running commands that update task files.
anti_patterns: Do not use vague tasks without files or acceptance criteria.
Do not run it against arbitrary files outside the project plan.
Do not mark a task complete before verification.

faq.question: What file format does this skill expect?
faq.answer: It expects a Markdown document with an Implementation Tasks section and checkbox task items.

faq.question: How does it choose the next task?
faq.answer: It selects pending tasks whose dependencies are complete, then chooses the lowest priority number.

faq.question: Can it resume interrupted work?
faq.answer: Yes. It reads the existing checkboxes and continues from the first available pending task.

faq.question: Does it run tests automatically?
faq.answer: The workflow asks the agent to verify acceptance criteria. Test commands depend on the project.

faq.question: Can it edit project files?
faq.answer: The skill can guide implementation work. Its helper script directly updates the selected Markdown task file.

faq.question: Is it safe for untrusted task files?
faq.answer: No. Review task files first because they can direct broad implementation changes.
